title: Spark's Ecosystem Upkeep Fee is charged on market capitalization rather than on revenue or profit
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.3.1.2.1.1.1 sets the terms of Spark's Ecosystem Upkeep Fee Primitive Instance: "Spark will pay 0.50% of its market capitalization per year in USDS."

The choice of base is the design decision, not the rate. A fee on revenue or profit would flex with performance and be reducible through accounting discretion; a fee on market capitalization tracks the *value the ecosystem's support has created* and is computed from an external, hard-to-manipulate number. An Agent that grows in market value pays more for upkeep even if it is unprofitable.

That is deliberately a hard obligation. It behaves like a carrying cost on the Agent's existence rather than a share of its earnings, so it penalizes valuation without cash generation and cannot be minimized by reinvesting everything. Denominating it in USDS also makes the payment a source of standing USDS demand rather than a transfer of the Agent's own token.

The fee is live but its mechanics are not: A.6.1.1.1.2.3.1.2.1.2.1.1 says "the process to pay 0.50% of Spark's market capitalization per year in USDS will be specified in future iterations of the Spark Artifact." The obligation exists without a defined measurement window, valuation source, or payment cadence — leaving the material questions (which market cap, measured when) open.
description: 0.50% of market cap per year, payable in USDS — a levy that scales with the Agent's valuation and falls due regardless of whether the Agent earned anything.
